key_insight: Simple propagation-based baselines can recover much of the performance of complex relational deep learning models when they exploit neighborhood-filtered features and historical labels.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners, this suggests a cheaper, easier-to-debug alternative to heterogeneous GNNs/Transformers may be strong enough for many relational database prediction tasks.
method: Apply fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs.
Train an MLP on the propagated features for target prediction.
Refine predictions with Correct-and-Smooth using a task-specific meta-graph over target entities.
evidence_signal: On RelBench classification and regression tasks, an MLP on neighborhood-filtered features outperformed target-only features on most tasks and recovered a substantial portion of heterogeneous GNN performance.
watch_item: Correct-and-Smooth depends on a separately constructed meta-graph, since target-entity connections are not directly available in the relational entity graph.
paper_title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
